Mira: Heads-up 1: I'd like to align on three pilot lanes for the Optimize toolkit this week. Goal: pick owners, concrete acceptance checks, and one short experiment per lane. Quick reads only, please react with :eyes: if you can review.

Ethan: On it. Drop the lanes here and I'll comment.

Mira: Lane A (low-latency chat): streaming required, p99 target < 150ms, customers care about response fluidity. Cost-savings target >= 20%. Small in-memory KV prefix cache expected.

Lina: This lane needs careful cache invalidation rules. Also flagging quant risk: 4-bit may change subtle token probabilities -> hallucination.

Mira: Lane B (bulk embeddings): nightly/weekly jobs, throughput-first. Aim for ~10x cost reduction. Aggressive quant okay if recall stays within 1% of baseline.

Devon: For embeddings, 8-bit looks low-risk; 4-bit could be OK if we validate on a representative corpus. Need auto-fallback if evals fail.

Mira: Lane C (private/regulatory): single-tenant or VPC, accuracy must match baseline within 0.5% F1, full audit logs, KMS integration required. Quant only with signed-off regressions.

Kai: Ops note: private lanes require explicit cache persistence and eviction SLAs. We'll need an ops checklist.

Mira: Proposed owners: Ethan -> A, Devon -> B, Kai -> C. Please reply with: 1) short acceptance criteria (metrics + thresholds), 2) top 2 risks, 3) one de-risking experiment we can run in 2 weeks.

Ethan: A acceptance: p95 < 60ms, p99 < 150ms, streaming latency tail within 10% of baseline, quality regen rate < 1%. Risks: cache races under concurrent updates, quant-induced subtle errors. Experiment: staged traffic test toggling prefix cache (on/off) + small adaptive batching; run a 1k-turn eval set focused on hallucinations.

Devon: B acceptance: end-to-end throughput >= target to hit 10x cost drop, embedding recall delta <= 1% on benchmark. Risks: distribution shift for long-tail queries, bench mismatch vs customer dataset. Experiment: run 200k sample job across 8-bit and 4-bit models, compare recall/NN overlap; wire eval-triggered alert to disable quant if recall drop >0.5% over 2 runs.

Kai: C acceptance: customer F1 within 0.5% vs baseline, successful KMS/HSM key ops, deployment runbook passes automation checks. Risks: tenant-specific eval variance, KMS failures delaying rollouts. Experiment: per-tenant canary where we enable quant + run customer's eval for 50 queries; if drop >0.3% in 3 consecutive canaries -> automatic rollback and page SRE.

Mira: Great. Next item: we need a minimal "eval-triggered alert" prototype everyone can agree on. Draft something short and operational: metric, threshold, cadence, action.

Ethan: Draft: metric = primary eval (F1 for search, recall@k for embeddings, hallucination score for chat). Trigger = metric drops >0.3% vs last successful run for 3 consecutive runs. Cadence = nightly for batch lane, per-deploy + nightly for realtime lane. Action = 1) soft alert (email/console) on first failure, 2) auto-disable quantized path and page oncall on third consecutive failure.

Devon: +1. Add roll-up telemetry export (sampled requests + model logits for failed runs) so we can triage. Also recommend a "grace period" after deploy: ignore first run if deploy caused obvious drift.

Kai: For private lane, change action to: immediate soft-alert + hold deployment (don't auto-disable across tenant without manual sign-off) because of compliance. Otherwise same cadence.

Mira: I like this. I'll write a one-pager with: lanes, owners, acceptance bullets, risks, experiment plans, and the alert proto. Will open pilot tickets and link them.

optimize-bot: Ticket created: OPT-8290 "Optimize pilot lanes: owners + acceptance checks" assigned to Mira. :robot_face:

Ethan: I'll start the A/B test config for lane A and post the playbook here.

Devon: I'll assemble the embedding benchmark sets (small/medium/long-tail) and share tomorrow.

Kai: I'll draft the private-lane ops checklist and KMS integration steps.

Mira: Thanks team. If no objections, I'll lock the scope by Fri and spin up the kickoff.

Ethan: No objections.

Devon: All good from me.

Kai: 44d

Mira: Closing thread for now — will ping when the one-pager is ready.
